previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and a history of dialysis access complications was admitted for worsening hand ischemia due to steal syndrome from her right upper extremity AV fistula. She underwent successful fistula banding to reduce blood flow and restore perfusion to her hand. Postoperatively, she was monitored for pain, circulation, and anticoagulation management, with warfarin held temporarily and restarted the following day. She received scheduled hemodialysis during admission with stable recovery, no complications, and resolution of ischemic symptoms. She was discharged home with instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, medications including short-term pain control and stool softener, and follow-up with the surgical team in two weeks.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms ___, 

It was a pleasure caring for you during your recent 
hospitalization.  You came in because of dizziness, difficulty 
walking, and confusion.  Neurology specialists saw you and felt 
that your sense of imbalance is most likely a chronic, 
multifactorial problem, for which there is unfortunately no 
specific treatment. It may be related to fluid shifts affecting 
the vestibular nerve (the nerve in the inner ear that controls 
balance), which can especially likely to happen with dialysis. 
Arthritis in the neck may also be contributing, due to mild 
compression of the nerves.  

Some things you can do to help relieve symptoms include:
- Maintaining your head in a neutral position at bedtime and 
during dialysis, wearing a cervical collar may assist with this, 
as may using a firm mattress and no/minimal pillows
-Wearing compression stockings during dialysis to increase the 
blood flow to your brain and prevent your blood pressure from 
dropping 

Physical therapy saw you and felt you are safe to walk around 
with a walker at home, and you will be set up with evaluation 
for home physical therapy.  

You also got hemodialysis on ___ and ___.  You 
will resume your dialysis as directed by Dr. ___.

You were seen by an opthalmologist for eye pain and they 
recommended antibiotic eye drops for 7 days, then you will 
follow up in clinic.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Dizziness.

COMPARISON:  CT head ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images through the brain were obtained without the
administration of IV contrast.  Coronal, sagittal thin section bone algorithm
reconstructed images were obtained.

FINDINGS:  No acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or acute
large territorial infarction.  Prominent extra-axial spaces in relation to the
patient's age.  Periventricular and subcortical white matter hypodensities
likely reflect chronic small vessel ischemic disease.

No fracture.  Mucosal thickening in the sphenoid sinus is slightly increased
compared to the prior study.  Increased opacification of the bilateral mastoid
air cells compared to the prior study.  The middle ear cavities are clear.  

IMPRESSION:  Increased mucosal thickening in the sphenoid sinuses and
increased opacification of the mastoid air cells bilatearlly may be due to an
inflammatory process.

HISTORY:  Dizziness.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest:  Frontal and lateral views.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

There are low lung volumes.  There is persistent elevation of the right
hemidiaphragm and overlying right base atelectasis.  Lingular atelectasis is
also seen.  There is blunting of the posterior left costophrenic angle
suggesting a small pleural effusion.  There is mild diffuse increase in
interstitial markings suggesting mild interstitial pulmonary edema.  The
cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are stable.

IMPRESSION:

Mild interstitial pulmonary edema and small left pleural effusion.
